controls_label: M5 diff-view and review-thread controls with change-kind, moved-versus-hidden context, source-versus-rendered truth, stable hunk identity, one thread-state vocabulary, comment-anchor durability, and provider-local-versus-provider-hosted parity aligned across editor, diff, review, notebook, support, and product surfaces

controls_rows.scope_summary: The editor names diff change kinds and moved-versus-hidden context with no collapsed generic change, and shows draft-versus-published review threads with one controlled vocabulary; both degrade honestly when a change kind is collapsed or a thread state is encoded by color alone

diff_examples.hunk_label: change shown only by a generic marker

thread_examples.comment_label: draft: consider extracting this into a helper
published: please add a test for the empty-input case
state shown only by a colored dot / provider jargon

controls_rows.scope_summary: The diff surface stays honest when context is moved, elided, collapsed, or re-anchored rather than pretending one immutable view, and degrades honestly when a moved region is hidden or collapsed context is not disclosed

diff_examples.hunk_label: modified: 4 lines changed (12 unchanged lines collapsed)
region actually moved but shown as an added/removed pair
hunk pretending a full view while context is collapsed

thread_examples.comment_label: resolved: fixed in the latest revision
re-anchored: comment reattached after an upstream edit

controls_rows.scope_summary: The review surface exposes the same thread-state grammar and anchor durability across desktop, browser handoff, and exported packets, keeps outdated and resolved distinct without color, and degrades honestly when the two are blurred or an anchor silently drifts

diff_examples.hunk_label: hunk with no resolvable context visibility

thread_examples.comment_label: outdated: the code below this comment has since moved
resolved: fixed in the latest revision
outdated thread reading the same as a resolved one
comment whose anchor silently drifted off its line

controls_rows.scope_summary: The notebook reuses the same diff and review-thread grammar in code cells, discloses a rebased hunk id rather than reading as stable, and degrades honestly when a hunk identity silently drifts or a draft reads as published

diff_examples.hunk_label: added: cell edit (hunk id rebased onto latest run)
hunk whose identity silently drifted between runs

thread_examples.comment_label: locked: this thread is locked pending a decision
unsent draft presented as if already published

controls_rows.scope_summary: The support export carries the same resolved diff and thread truth, so a rendered-versus-source blur, an opaque summary, an implicit provider locality, or an unstated identity is visible in evidence rather than hidden behind compact chrome

diff_examples.hunk_label: modified: rendered preview (approximate; open source for exact bytes)
transformed preview presented as the exact source bytes
diff whose summary is an opaque blob with no structure

thread_examples.comment_label: pending send: queued but not yet published to the provider
comment leaving provider-local vs hosted implicit on export

controls_rows.scope_summary: In-product surfaces reuse the same diff and thread grammar a user sees in the editor, always offering the command-backed detail path and degrading honestly when the trace path is missing, the rendering or hunk identity is unresolved, or the provider locality is unresolved

diff_examples.hunk_label: hunk with no command-backed detail path
hunk with no resolvable source-versus-rendered relationship

thread_examples.comment_label: draft: consider extracting this into a helper
comment with no resolvable thread state
comment with no resolvable anchor durability
comment with no resolvable provider locality
